title: The Right Memory in the Wrong Context: Verifying Retrieval Admissibility in Long-Term Agent Memory

object.carrier: Long-term agent memory records from RHELM and MemOps benchmarks, carrying released governance metadata: trusted namespace/provenance identifiers (authenticated account, persona, profile, tenant, or project), policy fields, and lifecycle states (current/stale/superseded)

safety_property.statement: A memory retrieved as relevant to a query must also be admissible for the current principal, purpose/policy, intent, and time; relevance-based recall and final-answer accuracy cannot reveal whether another principal's record, a policy-violating record, or a superseded/forgotten record crossed the prompt boundary, nor whether required eligible evidence was withheld.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Three-valued (admissible/inadmissible/unresolved) per-record labels on scope, policy, and lifecycle axes combined by strong Kleene conjunction; matched-recall partial-identification bounds and typed violation exposure rates on feasible matched prefixes at target recall .8; memory-ID tracking through prompt exposure; and literal-marker target disclosure scoring in agent answers.

capabilities: No live adversary in the main studies; failures arise from context mismatch (wrong principal, policy violation, superseded/forgotten state) in ordinary retrieval
Robustness stress tests only: method-visible metadata corruption (namespace false-deny/false-allow/missing/swaps, policy and lifecycle label errors) injected at eight nested rates over ten seeds
assumptions: Namespaces are trusted provenance identifiers rather than inferred from text; under complete trusted namespace labels and unchanged within-namespace scores, namespace pre-filtering cannot worsen a released anchor's rank
Released governance fields (scope, policy, lifecycle state) are available and treated as released-field consistency rather than independently adjudicated ground truth
Readers are stateless and receive only the question and ordered memory IDs/text, blinded to route identity and scores; a blinded judge scores answers
not_covered: Adversarial attacks on memory content or provenance in deployment; corruption channels are simulated grid brackets, not safety thresholds
Graph-structured selectors where unauthenticated structural writes can alter which authenticated records are selected; support result assumes flat candidate sets and trusted support labels
Gold-aware over-refusal, internal causal use of evidence, model ranking, safety certification, or generalization beyond tested corruption channels
Wall-clock latency claims (hardware records incomplete; similarity-evaluation counts are query-candidate score computations)

intervention.name: Trusted namespace (provenance) candidate-support restriction within a retrieval-admissibility verification framework
intervention.description: Restricts retrieval candidate support to memories carrying the query's trusted namespace label before semantic ranking (dense embedding), evaluated post-hoc against global dense, recency+dense, random same-size partitions, late global post-filtering, threshold/cluster routers, released-field governance gates, and text-only LLM verifiers; a three-valued admissibility audit then scores scope/policy/lifecycle violations at matched required-evidence recall and follows memory IDs through prompt exposure to answer-level disclosure.

results.claim: On frozen top-20 rankings of 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries, restricting candidate support to the trusted namespace raises anchor recall and 80%-recall feasibility relative to global dense retrieval.
results.setting: Post-hoc top-20 reanalysis of frozen dense rankings (Qwen3-Embedding-8B), 3,767 recall-evaluable RHELM/MemOps evaluation queries, equal-source macro average, target recall .8, no adversary
results.quote: Namespace support raises top-20 recall .432 to .533 and feasibility .237 to .311 (Table 2a).

results.claim: Namespace restriction lowers both endpoints of the admissibility partial-identification bounds on feasible matched prefixes at .992 label coverage.
results.setting: Post-hoc top-20 admissibility audit on frozen rankings, 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries, scope+policy+lifecycle target, equal-source macro
results.quote: Both bound endpoints decrease from [.187,.195] to [.118,.126] at .992 coverage.

results.claim: Namespace pre-filtering cuts exact similarity evaluations by roughly two orders of magnitude versus global dense while achieving the higher recall (58.1x fewer per the delta row).
results.setting: Frozen top-20 audit, 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries; work counted as query-candidate score computations, not wall-clock latency
results.quote:
| Global dense | text | .432 | .237 | [.187,.195] | .798 | 90,122 |
| Global recency+dense | text + released order | .452 | .256 | [.198,.206] | .784 | 90,122 |
| Namespace dense | text + trusted namespace | .533 | .311 | [.118,.126] | .713 | 1,551 |

results.claim: Trusted namespace support eliminates wrong-scope (other-principal) typed exposure in feasible matched prefixes under complete trusted labels, while policy-disallowed exposure slightly rises and lifecycle-incompatible exposure is nearly unchanged.
results.setting: Feasible matched prefixes at tau=.8 on frozen top-20 rankings, 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries; typed axes can overlap
results.quote:
| Route | Wrong scope ↓\downarrow | Policy-disallowed ↓\downarrow | Lifecycle-incompatible ↓\downarrow |
| Global dense | .084 | .094 | .019 |
| Namespace dense | .000 | .101 | .017 |

results.claim: Across 1,523 paired benchmark-native cases, namespace routing is associated with judged-accuracy gains for all three readers, but recall also changes, so the route-to-reader comparison is observational rather than causal.
results.metric: judged answer accuracy gain (namespace minus global)
results.setting: 1,523 paired RHELM/MemOps reader cases (523 RHELM + 1,000 MemOps sample), readers DeepSeek V4 Pro / Gemini 3.6 Flash / gated GPT-5.6 Luna, shared blinded Claude Haiku 4.5 judge, no reader pooling
results.quote: Across 1,523 paired benchmark-native cases, namespace routing is associated with judged-accuracy gains of 0.053–0.068 across three readers; recall also changes, so this comparison is observational.

results.claim: Text-only LLM verifiers are near chance at eligibility decisions (ROC-AUC .626/.522 for GPT-5.6 Sol / Gemini 3.6 Flash) and, at the 1% required-anchor false-denial limit, detect no violations.
results.setting: 72 held-out development analysis cases with fixed top-20 pools; GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.6 Flash as text-only verifiers; at the 1% required-anchor false-denial limit GPT-5.6 Sol detects nothing and no Gemini 3.6 Flash threshold qualifies
results.quote: Their ROC-AUC is .626/.522 and required-anchor false denial is .059/.020.

results.claim: A label-aligned released-metadata reference gate preserves required evidence, lowering constrained loss .032 with unchanged recall and feasibility, in contrast to the text-only verifiers which lower recall/feasibility.
results.setting: 72 held-out development cases, fixed top-20 pools, released-field deterministic reference control (not an independently validated governance predictor)
results.quote: On 72 held-out development cases, the label-aligned reference lowers loss .032 with unchanged recall/feasibility.

results.claim: In the 16 controlled exposure scenarios, only DeepSeek V4 Pro shows a relevant-inadmissible exposure effect on literal target disclosure whose 95% CI excludes zero (+.156 [.031,.312]); the other three readers' contrasts are .000/.000/+.125, a reader-specific exact-marker effect, not a safety guarantee.
results.setting: 16 constructed scenarios (4 per relevance-admissibility cell), 192 paired units and 384 stateless requests per reader; readers GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.6 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, plus unpooled Claude Opus 5 replication
results.quote: corresponding relevant-inadmissible literal-disclosure contrasts are .000/.000/+.156/+.125. Only DeepSeek V4 Pro excludes zero (95% CI [.031,.312]).

limitations.statement: Evidence base is narrow: two public benchmarks with only seven RHELM evaluation groups, and namespaces are trusted labels rather than inferred.
limitations.quote: The evidence covers two public sources and only seven RHELM groups; namespaces are trusted rather than inferred.

limitations.statement: Human governance labels are only a repeatability sample, with weak agreement on prohibited status, so that axis is released-field consistency rather than adjudicated truth.
limitations.quote: Human labels are a repeatability sample, with weak prevalence-corrected agreement for prohibited status.

limitations.statement: Candidate-count reductions are not wall-clock latency claims because source-execution hardware records are incomplete.
limitations.quote: Source-execution hardware records are incomplete, so candidate-count reductions are not wall-clock latency claims.

limitations.statement: The study does not establish gold-aware over-refusal, internal causal use of evidence, a model ranking, safety certification, or generalization beyond the tested corruption channels.
limitations.quote: We do not establish gold-aware over-refusal, internal use, a model ranking, safety certification, or generalization beyond the tested corruption channels.

limitations.statement: The frozen-route reader comparison is associational; only the constructed 16-scenario exposure study randomizes prompt exposure.
limitations.quote: The frozen-route reader comparison is associational; only the constructed exposure study randomizes prompt exposure under its stated scenarios.

limitations.statement: The support result does not cover graph-structured selectors in which unauthenticated structural writes can alter which authenticated records are selected.
limitations.quote: We also do not cover graph-structured selectors in which unauthenticated structural writes can alter which authenticated records are selected; our support result assumes flat candidate sets and trusted support labels
